stem: On what date is Unity Day commemorated in Zimbabwe?

options.rationale: Correct: the Unity Accord was signed on 22 December 1987.
18 April is Independence Day.
25 May is Africa Day.
12 September 1890 is when the Pioneer Column reached Fort Salisbury; it is not Unity Day.

explanation: Unity Day, 22 December, marks the Unity Accord of 1987.

stem: Africa Day on 25 May commemorates the founding of which organisation?

options.rationale: Correct: the OAU was founded on 25 May 1963.
SADC was formed in 1992.
The UN was founded on 24 October 1945.

options.content: the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa
options.rationale: COMESA's treaty dates from 1993.

explanation: The OAU was founded in Addis Ababa on 25 May 1963; the African Union replaced it in 2002.

options.rationale: 18 April is Independence Day.

options.content: on the second Monday of August
options.rationale: Correct: the date changes each year but is always the second Monday of August.

options.content: on the first Saturday of December
options.rationale: This is National Tree Planting Day.
This is Unity Day.

explanation: Heroes Day is the second Monday of August, followed by Defence Forces Day on the Tuesday.

stem: Which two parties signed the Unity Accord commemorated on Unity Day?

options.rationale: The Rhodesian Front was the party of the settler government before 1980.
The Accord was between Zimbabwean parties.
Correct: the two main nationalist parties united in 1987.
FRELIMO is a Mozambican party.

explanation: The Unity Accord of 22 December 1987 united ZANU (PF) and PF-ZAPU and ended the conflict of the 1980s.

stem: Where is the main national ceremony held on Heroes Day?

options.content: the Great Zimbabwe monument near Masvingo
options.rationale: Great Zimbabwe is a pre-colonial monument.
This is a natural World Heritage Site.

options.content: the National Heroes Acre in Harare
options.rationale: Correct: the main ceremony is at the National Heroes Acre.
Chimoio is commemorated on 23 November.

explanation: The main Heroes Day ceremony takes place at the National Heroes Acre; provinces and districts hold their own.

stem: On a December Saturday, pupils at a school in Marondera each plant an indigenous tree and agree a watering rota. Which national event are they observing?

options.rationale: Unity Day (22 December) is about national unity, not trees.
Correct: it falls on the first Saturday of December.
Independence Day is on 18 April and is not about trees.
Africa Day is on 25 May.

explanation: National Tree Planting Day, the first Saturday of December, encourages planting and caring for trees.
hints: Which event is about the environment?

stem: Which statement **best** explains why Defence Forces Day follows Heroes Day?

options.content: The defence forces were founded before the liberation struggle began
options.rationale: The Zimbabwe Defence Forces were formed after independence.

options.content: There was not enough space in the national calendar to hold it in any other month of the year
options.rationale: The timing is deliberate, not about space.

options.content: Soldiers are not allowed to attend Heroes Day ceremonies
options.rationale: Soldiers take part in Heroes Day ceremonies.

options.content: It links honouring those who won independence with the forces that now defend it
options.rationale: Correct: the two days connect past sacrifice and present defence.

explanation: Heroes Day honours those who sacrificed for independence; Defence Forces Day recognises the forces that defend it.
hints: Think of what was won and who protects it.

stem: A community is planning Unity Day. Some older residents lost relatives in the conflict of the 1980s. Which approach **best** serves the purpose of the day?

options.content: Forbid any mention of the 1980s so that the celebration stays cheerful
options.rationale: Silence can deepen hurt and does not promote reconciliation.

options.content: Hold separate events for each language group so that people from different areas never have to meet
options.rationale: Separate events work against the aim of unity.

options.content: Cancel the event because past conflict makes unity impossible
options.rationale: The Accord shows that unity can follow conflict.

options.content: Celebrate unity while respectfully acknowledging the suffering that came before the Accord
options.rationale: Correct: honest remembrance supports reconciliation.

explanation: Unity Day is about peace and national unity; acknowledging past suffering honestly supports healing.

stem: Independence Day is celebrated on 18 April.
explanation: True. Zimbabwe became independent on 18 April 1980.

stem: Heroes Day falls on the same date every year.
explanation: False. Heroes Day is the second Monday of August, so its date changes from year to year.

stem: Match each national event with what it commemorates.

right.content: the 1987 Accord between two nationalist parties
the founding of the OAU in 1963
the end of colonial rule in 1980
those who sacrificed in the liberation struggle

explanation: Independence Day: 1980; Heroes Day: the heroes of the struggle; Unity Day: the Accord of 1987; Africa Day: the OAU of 1963.

payload.template: Defence Forces Day is held on the {{blank:a}} after Heroes Day. National Tree Planting Day is held on the first Saturday of {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Defence Forces Day is the Tuesday after Heroes Day; Tree Planting Day is the first Saturday of December.

stem: State **four** ways in which Independence Day is celebrated.

points.description: Any one of: national celebrations at a stadium; raising the flag; speeches; music and dance; parades; sports competitions; church services and prayers; community and school celebrations
A second different way
A third different way
A fourth different way

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There are national celebrations at a stadium with the raising of the flag and speeches; musicians and dancers perform; there are sports competitions; and churches hold services of thanksgiving.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why citizens should take part in national events.

points.description: Identifies unity
Develops: people of all backgrounds celebrate together, strengthening their sense of one nation
Identifies remembrance / patriotism / education
Develops: e.g. honouring heroes keeps their sacrifice alive for young people, or celebrating independence builds pride in the country

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Taking part brings together people of every language, region and faith, so they feel part of one nation. It also keeps alive the memory of those who sacrificed for independence, so young people learn the history and grow up proud of their country.

explanation: One mark for each reason and one for its development.
hints: Think of what an event does for the people who attend.

stem: Few young people in a fictional ward in Gwanda attended last year's Heroes Day ceremony. Suggest **two** ways the ward could involve more young people, and explain each.

points.description: Suggests involving schools and youth groups (poems, drama, history quizzes, music) in the programme
Explains that young people come when they have an active part and learn the history in an engaging way
Suggests inviting veterans or elders to share their stories, or using social media and radio to announce the event
Explains that personal stories make the history real / good publicity reaches young people where they are

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The ward could invite schools and youth groups to perform poems, drama and music about the struggle, because young people attend when they have an active part. It could also invite veterans and elders to share their stories, and announce the event on community radio and social media, so that young people hear about it and find the history real and interesting.

explanation: One mark for each sensible suggestion and one for explaining it.
hints: Think of what would make a young person want to come.

stem:
The table shows the results of a survey of 100 Form 3 pupils at a school in Kariba, asking which national event they took part in during the year (invented for this question; pupils could choose more than one event).

| National event | Pupils who took part |
|---|---|
| Independence Day | 72 |
| Heroes Day | 40 |
| National Tree Planting Day | 55 |
| Unity Day | 12 |
| Africa Day | 18 |

Study the table and answer the questions.

options.rationale: 18 pupils took part in Africa Day.
40 pupils took part in Heroes Day.
This had the highest participation.
Correct: only 12 pupils took part.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** reasons why participation in Unity Day was low.

points.description: It falls on 22 December, during the school holidays, when pupils are away from school
Pupils may know little about the Unity Accord / fewer events are organised for it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Unity Day falls on 22 December, in the school holidays, so the school cannot organise an event. Many pupils also know little about the Unity Accord, and fewer public events are held for it.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Suggest how the school could increase awareness of Unity Day, and explain why this matters.

points.description: Hold a Unity Day lesson or assembly before the schools close in December
Organise activities that bring together pupils of different backgrounds (cultural day, debates)
Explains that knowing about the Accord teaches peace and tolerance and strengthens national unity

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The school could hold a Unity Day assembly and lesson before closing in December, and organise a cultural day where pupils of different backgrounds share songs and food. This matters because learning about the Accord teaches peace and tolerance and helps pupils see themselves as one nation.

explanation: A data-response practice item on participation in national events.
hints: Check the date of Unity Day against the school calendar.

stem: This question is about national events in Zimbabwe.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe how Heroes Day is commemorated.

points.description: Main ceremony at the National Heroes Acre in Harare
Ceremonies at provincial and district heroes acres
Laying of wreaths and speeches honouring the heroes
Music, prayers or a minute of silence; it is a public holiday followed by Defence Forces Day

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The main ceremony is held at the National Heroes Acre in Harare, and provinces and districts hold ceremonies at their own heroes acres. Wreaths are laid on the graves and speeches honour those who sacrificed in the liberation struggle. There are prayers, music and moments of silence, and the day is a public holiday followed by Defence Forces Day.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: "National events are an effective way of building national unity." How far do you agree?

points.description: For: people of all backgrounds gather and celebrate together; shared memory and pride
For: education of the young; Unity Day directly promotes reconciliation
Against: some people do not attend or feel left out; events can be seen as costly or one-sided; one day cannot remove deep divisions or economic hardship
Supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
National events can build unity. On Independence Day people of every language, region and faith celebrate together, and Heroes Day gives the nation a shared memory of sacrifice. School activities teach young people the history behind the events, and Unity Day directly promotes peace and reconciliation.

However, events alone have limits. Many people do not attend, especially in remote areas or when they are struggling to earn a living. Some feel that certain events do not tell the whole story or do not include them, and some question the cost. A single day cannot heal deep divisions or end poverty and inequality.

I partly agree. National events are a useful way of building unity because they give citizens shared memories and pride, but they work best when they are inclusive and honest about the past, and when unity is also built through fairness in everyday life.

explanation: A practice evaluative item on national events and national unity.
hints: In (b), weigh what events achieve against what they cannot do alone.
